text:
zoe_support: Customer reports intermittent SSE stream truncation after long idle (~90-150s). They see final chunk missing or a partial JSON object and client reconnects. Happening only when traffic flows: Client -> Cloudflare -> ALB -> nginx origin.

mike_runtime: Do we have any traces? Is it always the last chunk or sometimes mid-stream?

zoe_support: Mostly the last chunk after a long idle. If the client keeps connection active, stream is fine. Repro steps from customer: 1) Start SSE request, receive a few events. 2) Wait ~2m, trigger new event on server. 3) Client gets reconnect; last event never arrives or arrives truncated.

anna_netops: Sounds like idle timeout or connection half-close. ALB default idle timeout is 60s, CF fronting may have its own keepalive. Any TCP RST/FIN in pcap?

zoe_support: Customer provided logs — here is the HTTP request they used to test:

```
curl -v -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  -H "Cache-Control: no-cache" \
  "https://api.customer.example/stream?session=abc123"
```

Response headers from origin (nginx): `HTTP/1.1 200 OK`, `Content-Type: text/event-stream`, `Transfer-Encoding: chunked`, `Connection: keep-alive`.

raj_devex: Can you paste sample SSE payload showing truncation? Even a small truncated last line helps.

zoe_support: Example (what client received):

```
data: {"id":"evt-42","text":"processing complete","meta":{...}}
data: {"id":"evt-43","text":"partial",
```
The second event ends mid-object. Origin logs show event emitted fully.

mike_runtime: Two likely classes: 1) Proxy buffering coalescing last-chunk and then connection closed mid-chunk; 2) TLS session resume/half-close at Cloudflare causing downstream FIN seen by origin. Both can produce truncation.

anna_netops: Customer said they use Cloudflare Spectrum for proxying TLS, and ALB sits between CF and origin. ALB idle timeout can close first, then CF tries to re-use connection and we see misordering. We should check ALB access logs for close reason.

zoe_support: I asked customer for tcpdump from origin. They attached a short pcap showing a FIN from ALB ~5s after server wrote final chunk, then client reported truncated payload.

mike_runtime: If FIN happens after we wrote but before kernel flushed last bytes to socket, that could cause TCP partial delivery. Can they reproduce with keepalive pings from server (single-space heartbeat every 20s)?

jay_cust_success: Customer concerned about billing and analytics — reconnections causing duplicate events and overcounting. Need a clear mitigation ASAP.

raj_devex: Short-term workaround suggestions: a) send heartbeat comment lines `: heartbeat\n\n` every 20s to keep proxies from idling; b) set `Connection: close` to avoid reusing pooled connections (not ideal); c) increase ALB idle timeout to 300s while we investigate.

anna_netops: Also check nginx `proxy_buffering` — if enabled it can buffer and then send a large chunk which looks like truncation if connection resets. On origin set `proxy_buffering off; chunked_transfer_encoding on;` and `sendfile off` to ensure immediate flush.

zoe_support: Customer tried `proxy_buffering off` but ALB still closed connection. They increased ALB idle timeout to 180s and saw fewer incidents but not eliminated.

mike_runtime: Ask them to instrument with a tiny server loop that writes `data: ping\n\n` every 25s and see if it stabilizes. If it does, it's definitely an idle timeout at the proxy layer.

zoe_support: They ran heartbeat test — stable for 6k requests with heartbeat every 25s, failures resumed when heartbeat stopped.

mike_runtime: Good repro. Next step: capture server-side socket state at write time (SO_LINGER, write return codes). Also check for TLS renegotiation or session resumption events on Cloudflare side.

cf_bot: Cloudflare note: edge connection pooling can reuse TLS sessions; for long-lived streams, enable "origin keepalive" and consider Worker-based streaming to avoid connection pooling.

anna_netops: We should coordinate with CF to see whether they sent a TCP-level RST when reusing backend connections. Also search ALB logs for `elb_status_code` or `target_status_code` around truncation times.

zoe_support: Action items asked of customer: 1) Keep heartbeat enabled for now. 2) Provide tcpdump/pcap from origin and ALB logs for a failing trace. 3) Tell us if they can temporarily route traffic bypassing Cloudflare to confirm CF involvement.

jay_cust_success: Customer agreed to bypass CF for a short window tomorrow at 09:00 PT. I'll coordinate.

raj_devex: Also suggest a server-side defensive change: emit events with an explicit sequence id and idempotency token so client can detect duplicates and incomplete events and reconcile after reconnect. Not a fix but mitigates billing/dup count issues.

mike_runtime: Long-term: we should document recommended SSE deployment topology for customers behind ALB+CF: align keepalives (CF -> ALB -> origin) to the same value, disable aggressive connection pooling, and recommend heartbeat interval < min idle timeout / 2. Add sample nginx and ALB configs to docs.

zoe_support: I'll create a support ticket with attachments and requested logs and escalate to eng-runtime if ALB/CF traces show mid-chunk close. Ticket: SUP-2026-314 (internal).

anna_netops: Thx. If we get a pcap showing `FIN` immediately after write, we can reproduce in lab by simulating ALB idle close. I can try that later today.

zoe_support: Thanks everyone. Will update thread after CF bypass test. :thumbsup:

jay_cust_success: Marking high priority due to billing impact. cc @account-manager

zoe_support: (after bypass test) quick update — bypassing CF eliminated the truncation entirely for the test window. Customer happy to keep heartbeat and then we pursue long-term CF/ALB tuning.

mike_runtime: Great. Please add a short KB entry linking to this thread and config snippets so others can find recommended settings.

zoe_support: Will do. Closing escalation after KB publish unless customer reopens.
